entries.originalText: Jesus hath many lovers of His heavenly kingdom, but few bearers of His Cross.
entries.modernizedText: Jesus has many lovers of His heavenly kingdom, but few bearers of His Cross.

entries.originalText: He hath many seekers of comfort, but few of tribulation.
entries.modernizedText: He has many seekers of comfort, but few of tribulation.

entries.originalText: He findeth many companions of His table, but few of His fasting.
entries.modernizedText: He finds many companions of His table, but few of His fasting.

entries.originalText: All desire to rejoice with Him, few are willing to undergo anything for His sake.
entries.modernizedText: All desire to rejoice with Him; few are willing to undergo anything for His sake.

entries.originalText: Many follow Jesus that they may eat of His loaves, but few that they may drink of the cup of His passion.
entries.modernizedText: Many follow Jesus so that they may eat of His loaves, but few so that they may drink of the cup of His passion.

entries.originalText: Many are astonished at His Miracles, few follow after the shame of His Cross.
entries.modernizedText: Many are astonished at His Miracles; few follow after the shame of His Cross.

entries.originalText: Many love Jesus so long as no adversities happen to them.
entries.modernizedText: Many love Jesus as long as no adversities happen to them.

entries.originalText: Many praise Him and bless Him, so long as they receive any comforts from Him.
entries.modernizedText: Many praise Him and bless Him as long as they receive any comforts from Him.

entries.originalText: But if Jesus hide Himself and withdraw from them a little while, they fall either into complaining or into too great dejection of mind.
entries.modernizedText: But if Jesus hides Himself and withdraws from them a little while, they fall either into complaining or into excessive dejection of mind.

entries.originalText: But they who love Jesus for Jesus’ sake, and not for any consolation of their own, bless Him in all tribulation and anguish of heart as in the highest consolation.
entries.modernizedText: But those who love Jesus for Jesus’ sake and not for any consolation of their own bless Him in all tribulation and anguish of heart as in the highest consolation.

entries.originalText: And if He should never give them consolation, nevertheless they would always praise Him and always give Him thanks.
entries.modernizedText: And if He should never give them consolation, nevertheless they would always praise Him and always give Him thanks.

entries.originalText: Oh what power hath the pure love of Jesus, unmixed with any gain or love of self!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, what power the pure love of Jesus has, unmixed with any gain or love of self!

entries.originalText: Should not all they be called mercenary who are always seeking consolations?
entries.modernizedText: Should not all those who are always seeking consolations be called mercenary?

entries.originalText: Do they not prove themselves lovers of self more than of Christ who are always seeking their own gain and advantage?
entries.modernizedText: Do those who are always seeking their own gain and advantage not prove themselves lovers of self more than of Christ?

entries.originalText: Where shall be found one who is willing to serve God altogether for nought?
entries.modernizedText: Where will one be found who is willing to serve God altogether for nothing?

entries.originalText: Rarely is any one found so spiritual as to be stripped of all selfish thoughts, for who shall find a man truly poor in spirit and free of all created things?
entries.modernizedText: Rarely is anyone found so spiritual as to be stripped of all selfish thoughts, for who will find a person truly poor in spirit and free of all created things?

entries.originalText: “His value is from afar, yea from the ends of the earth.”
entries.modernizedText: “His value is from afar, indeed from the ends of the earth.”

entries.originalText: A man may give away all his goods, yet that is nothing; and if he do many deeds of penitence, yet that is a small thing; and though he understand all knowledge, yet that is afar off; and if he have great virtue and zealous devotion, yet much is lacking unto him, yea, one thing which is the most necessary to him of all.
entries.modernizedText: A person may give away all his goods, yet that is nothing; and if he does many deeds of penitence, yet that is a small thing; and though he understands all knowledge, yet that is far off; and if he has great virtue and zealous devotion, yet much is lacking to him, indeed, one thing that is the most necessary of all to him.

entries.originalText: What is it then?
entries.modernizedText: What is it then?

entries.originalText: That having given up all things besides, he give up himself and go forth from himself utterly, and retain nothing of self-love; and having done all things which he knoweth to be his duty to do, that he feel that he hath done nothing.
entries.modernizedText: That having given up all things besides, he give up himself and go forth from himself utterly, retaining nothing of self-love; and having done all things he knows to be his duty, that he feel he has done nothing.

entries.originalText: Let him not reckon that much which might be much esteemed, but let him pronounce himself to be in truth an unprofitable servant, as the Truth Himself saith, When ye have done all things that are commanded you, say, we are unprofitable servants.(1) Then may he be truly poor and naked in spirit, and be able to say with the Prophet, As for me, I am poor and needy.(2) Nevertheless, no man is richer than he, no man stronger, no man freer.
entries.modernizedText: Let him not count as much what might be highly esteemed, but let him declare himself in truth an unprofitable servant, as the Truth Himself says, When you have done all things that are commanded you, say, we are unprofitable servants.(1) Then he may be truly poor and naked in spirit and be able to say with the Prophet, As for me, I am poor and needy.(2) Nevertheless, no one is richer than he, no one stronger, no one freer.

entries.originalText: For he knoweth both how to give up himself and all things, and how to be lowly in his own eyes.
entries.modernizedText: For he knows both how to give up himself and all things and how to be humble in his own eyes.
